sections.overview: This Orinoco eartheater also occurs in the Casiquiare and upper Negro headwaters of Venezuela.
sections.identification: A dark mark before the gill cover and seven parallel flank bars distinguish preserved specimens from other marked Geophagus.
sections.habitat: The description records it in blackwater tributaries and reaches of the Orinoco, Casiquiare and Negro headwaters.
sections.diet: By volume, a stomach-content study of 65 specimens found vegetable detritus at 36.1% and animal detritus at 27.0% of the diet.
sections.behavior: The taxonomic description focuses on identification and distribution rather than observed social behaviour.
sections.reproduction: The sources used here do not establish this species’ breeding behaviour.
sections.ecology: Unlike G. grammepareius and G. taeniopareius, which have a dark stripe from eye to preopercle, G. dicrozoster has a preopercular mark instead of that stripe.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global Least Concern assessment dated 28 October 2020.

sources.title: Geophagus abalios, G. dicrozoster and G. winemilleri: three new species from Venezuela — Zootaxa
